name: Substack
description: Substack is a publishing platform for writers, podcasters, video creators, and communities to distribute subscription-supported work through email, the web, and its apps.
agentUseSummary: Connect a customer-owned, access-approved Substack Developer API token, then let agents perform the API's single documented public creator-profile lookup by exact LinkedIn handle.

credentialRequirements.name: SUBSTACK_API_TOKEN
credentialRequirements.label: Substack Developer API token
credentialRequirements.helpText: Generate a token only after Substack approves the account for its Developer API. The current public guide does not document the token header, so provider-console acceptance must confirm the Bearer convention before release.

credentialRequirements.name: SUBSTACK_VALIDATION_LINKEDIN_HANDLE
credentialRequirements.label: Validation LinkedIn handle
credentialRequirements.helpText: A public LinkedIn profile handle used for the bounded connection check.

allowed.label: Search public creator profiles
allowed.description: Retrieve public Substack creator-profile summaries for one exact LinkedIn handle using Substack's only documented Developer API endpoint.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: The single public, read-only, exact-handle creator lookup runs directly; publication operations, private profiles, subscribers, posts, Notes, Chat, payments, writes, scraping, and raw access remain unavailable because Substack does not document them in its Developer API.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The same single public lookup runs directly; token secrecy, fixed origin, exact-handle validation, response bounds, conservative throttling, and audits remain mandatory.

providerSetup.blocker: Substack requires Developer API Terms acceptance, access approval that may take 7-10 business days, and a customer-generated token; its current public guide does not document token transport.
providerSetup.nextAction: Using the separate provider-console task, accept the Developer API Terms, obtain access approval and a disposable customer token, confirm the documented-at-runtime authentication header with Substack Support, then test exact-handle lookup, empty/multiple matches, bounds, throttling, token invalidation, disconnect, and post-disconnect denial before release.

evidence.supports: Substack documents account and Terms requirements, a 7-10-business-day access review, customer token generation, one GET profile/search/linkedin/{handle} endpoint, its public response fields, authenticity thresholds, empty/multiple matches, at-least-daily freshness, and unspecified rate limits. The published curl example omits token transport.

securityNotes: Relay exposes only Substack's one documented public, read-only exact-LinkedIn-handle lookup; it does not use undocumented private APIs, browser sessions, RSS scraping, or publisher operations.

The customer token is encrypted and server-side only. Relay's provisional Bearer transport must remain blocked from production until provider-console acceptance confirms it because the public guide does not name the token header.

Requests use only https://substack.com, reject redirects, validate the path segment, cap responses at 1 MB and ten matches, and conservatively allow one request per second while Substack publishes no numeric rate limit.
Results are public and may be self-reported, missing, multiple, authenticity-filtered, and at least one day stale; Relay preserves those caveats and never claims a guaranteed identity match.
Disconnect deletes Relay's encrypted token reference; Substack documents no token expiry, rotation, or remote revocation lifecycle in the current guide.
